clue.text: Lets in squiffy mum

indicators.note: squiffy means slightly drunk, so the words that follow stagger out of their proper order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lets their tipsy mother into the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother, but here it is the adjective, as in 'keep mum'.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep mum is to say nothing, so mum as an adjective means quiet and not speaking.

clue.text: Finished the prom piano act Verdi regularly forgot

indicators.note: forgetting at regular intervals drops every second letter of the run of words, keeping the rest

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and every other odd letter of these words

explanation.surface: A concert performer's Verdi piece kept slipping their mind, so the act ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Something terminated has been brought to an end, so the past participle matches finished in sense and form.

clue.text: Body part is viewed under infrared

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under something means coming after it in the column

blocks.note: IR is the standard abbreviation for infrared
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medical scan shows a part of the body under infrared light.
explanation.definitionFit: The coloured ring of the eye that controls the pupil is a part of the human body.

clue.text: Allure of tea: Mev finally buys case of matcha

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word next to it
a case is the outside shell, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: char is British slang for tea
the setter refers to himself
last letter of buys
first and last letters of matcha

explanation.surface: The setter is charmed by matcha tea and buys a box of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Mev is the setter's pseudonym, so his name stands for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling personal charm or attractiveness, which is what allure means.

clue.text: Patsy caught cable

definitions.note: the answer is the surname that goes with this first name

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a line is a wire or cable, as in a telephone line

explanation.surface: A fall guy is caught out by a cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patsy' reads as a dupe, but it is the first name of the American country singer Patsy Cline.
explanation.definitionFit: Patsy Cline was the American country singer of Crazy, so her surname completes the name given.

clue.text: Fashion brand takes control of new station

indicators.note: taking control of something means holding it, so the brand takes the next letter inside itself

blocks.note: the Paris fashion house
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A fashion house buys a controlling stake in a new broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A television or radio channel is also called a station, a single broadcast frequency or service.

clue.text: Places to sit and fish

blocks.note: first meaning: roosts where birds settle
second meaning: freshwater fish of a common family, in the plural

explanation.surface: A riverbank offers spots to sit and fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds settle on raised rails or branches, and the same word in the plural names several spiny freshwater fish.

clue.text: They get paid for work of person Lisa's corrupted

indicators.note: something corrupted has been spoiled and garbled, so these letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Paid workers are on the payroll of someone called Lisa who has gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlike amateurs, these people earn a living from their activity rather than doing it for nothing.

clue.text: Charlie enters certain city in South America

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: sure means certain
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man named Charlie arrives at a particular South American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sucre is the constitutional capital of Bolivia, a city in the south of that Andean nation.

clue.text: Made-up lady?

indicators.note: made up means invented or put together, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman wearing make-up, or a fictional heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Made-up also suits a pantomime dame, the man in heavy make-up playing a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A dame is a woman of rank or, informally, any woman, so it can stand for lady.

clue.text: Cher was in this low vehicle circumnavigating the poles

indicators.note: sailing all the way round something encloses it, so the vehicle goes around the next piece

blocks.note: to low is to make the sound a cow makes
a truck is a vehicle
north and south, the two poles

explanation.surface: A singer rode a lowered car around the world from pole to pole.
explanation.walkthrough: Cher won an Oscar for the 1987 romantic comedy Moonstruck.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1987 film starring Cher and Nicolas Cage won her the Academy Award for Best Actress.

clue.text: Example of canniest crackpot

indicators.note: a crackpot is someone mad, so the word before is treated in a crazy, scrambled way

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shrewd eccentric serves as a model case.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case or illustration of something, exactly what an example is.

clue.text: Sent back some people's sumptuous seafood serving

indicators.note: something sent back goes the opposite way, so the letters are read right to left
some means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: a run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Diners return a lavish platter of shellfish to the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A mussel is a shellfish commonly served as a dish, so one portion counts as a seafood serving.

clue.text: Storm noise disturbed pioneering educator

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A noisy storm unsettles an innovative teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria Montessori was an Italian physician who devised a child-centred method of early schooling still widely used.

clue.text: Note computer on spaceship undergoing retrograde motion

indicators.note: retrograde motion is movement backwards, so the name is read from the end

blocks.note: HAL 9000 is the computer aboard the spaceship in 2001: A Space Odyssey

explanation.surface: A message from a ship's computer while the craft drifts backwards in orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: In tonic sol-fa the sixth degree of the scale is spelt this way in British usage, a musical note.

clue.text: Electronic album O'Connor recorded in Hong Kong for IT dept?

indicators.note: something recorded in a place is put down inside it, so the pieces sit within the letters that follow

blocks.note: HK is the abbreviation for Hong Kong
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
an LP is a long-playing record album
Des O'Connor was a British TV entertainer and singer

explanation.surface: An entertainer cut an electronic record in Hong Kong for the computing department.
explanation.walkthrough: Des O'Connor was a long-serving British chat-show host and crooner. The question mark marks the definition as an example rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A help desk is the support service in an organisation, often the IT department, that answers user problems.

clue.text: Cathy who acts with presumably uncool tiny child

indicators.note: in can mean fashionable or cool, so being uncool suggests the word has lost that pair of letters

blocks.note: taken as written before the cut
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: An actress named Cathy works alongside an unfashionable little kid.
explanation.walkthrough: TINY loses IN, a word for cool or trendy, leaving TY. Cathy Tyson is a British actress known for the film Mona Lisa.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathy Tyson is an English actress, star of Mona Lisa and Band of Gold, so her surname fits.

clue.text: Sheep moves head and limb

indicators.note: moving the head shifts the leading letter to a new place, rearranging the word

blocks.note: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A sheep turns its head and stretches a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter moves back one place to become the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The arm is one of the upper limbs of the human body, from shoulder to hand.

clue.text: Married woman wraps English award for those in a group

indicators.note: to wrap something is to go all round it, so the first piece encloses the others

blocks.note: Mrs is the title of a married woman
E is the abbreviation for English
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A wife gift-wraps an English prize for everyone in the club.
explanation.walkthrough: The MBE is a British honour given by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Members are the people who belong to a club, society or other organised body.

clue.text: Perjurer rejected by journalist complained bitterly

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so the word is read in the other direction

blocks.note: a perjurer lies under oath
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A lying witness was turned away by a reporter and protested angrily.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to protest loudly and angrily, so the past tense means complained bitterly.

clue.text: Reed interrupts one of The Adverts audibly

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: an ad is one advert
Lou Reed was the Velvet Underground singer

explanation.surface: Lou Reed barges in on a member of the punk band The Adverts, making a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: The Adverts were a British punk band, but here the phrase means a single advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something so that it can be heard, rather than silently, is to say it audibly.

clue.text: Past pathetic Go form aside, finally succeed against adversity

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: over means past or finished
the last letters of these four words

explanation.surface: After a dismal run of results in the game of Go, a player brushes off bad form and wins.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcome is to defeat a difficulty or opponent, prevailing despite hardship.

clue.text: Arrest zero students occupying vehicle

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to be inside it, so these pieces sit within the next

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
O looks like zero
L stands for learner, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Police detain zero students who were squatting in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Collar is informal police slang for seizing or arresting a suspect.

clue.text: Glam rock band doctor diary about ultimate accolades

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the whole string before it runs backwards

blocks.note: Slade were a 1970s British glam rock group
MD is a doctor of medicine
a log is a diary or record

explanation.surface: A glam rock group's doctor keeps a diary about the band's top awards.
explanation.walkthrough: Slade were a 1970s British glam rock band, famous for Merry Xmas Everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold medals go to the winners at events like the Olympics, the highest honours available.

clue.text: Great record, almost cool

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
to ice is to cool

explanation.surface: An excellent record is very nearly cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic is informal praise meaning impressive or tremendous, so it can replace great as an adjective.

clue.text: Singer Lisa tucked in to sloe berries

indicators.note: something tucked in to other words is concealed within them, spanning the gap

blocks.note: letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A singer named Lisa tucks into some sloe berries.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisa Loeb is the American singer-songwriter whose hit Stay reached number one in 1994.

clue.text: Expel police officer's young lady

blocks.note: DI, a detective inspector, with the possessive S
a miss is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A detective's girlfriend is told to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss is to send away or discharge someone, as when expelling a pupil or sacking a worker.

clue.text: King rows and bellows

blocks.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
to oar a boat is to row it

explanation.surface: A monarch takes to the river and shouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' could be arguments, but here it is the verb for propelling a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, roars and bellows both describe giving a loud deep shout.
